chunks: And the peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I will be raised from the dead.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'peace be upon me the day I was born, and the day I die, and the day I will be raised'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often understood as addressing Prophet Isa (Jesus), son of Maryam, emphasizing his unique purity and the divine tranquility bestowed upon him from birth to resurrection. It underscores the concept of 'Salam' as a continuous state of spiritual safety and honor, reflecting the high status of the Ahl al-Bayt and prophets in Islamic tradition. The verse serves as a model for believers to seek peace in all stages of life, mirroring the prophetic experience.
